# TABLETS: THE PILL BOTTLE RANGE [italic]Sixteen tablets to an airtight bottle. All tablets are available over the dispensary counter unless marked. Follow the label, not your neighbour.[/italic]
## BICARIDINE
[bold]Red bottle.[/bold] For bruising, cuts and blunt injuries, and to help with bleeding. One tablet. Do not take more than two in a short period.
## KELOTANE
[bold]Yellow bottle.[/bold] For burns, from a hot pipe, a welding torch or a careless galley. One tablet. Do not take more than two in a short period. Cool the burn first.
## DYLOVENE
[bold]Green bottle.[/bold] An anti-toxin. For poisoning and for the after effects of bad air, bad water or bad food. One tablet. Do not take more than two in a short period.
## DEXALIN
[bold]Blue bottle.[/bold] For shortness of breath and oxygen starvation, after a suit leak, a smoke filled corridor or a seal that gave way. One tablet. Do not take more than two in a short period. Get to clean air first.
## INAPROVALINE
[bold]Purple bottle.[/bold] Helps steady a badly injured patient while help is on the way. One tablet. No more than four in a short period. Then get the patient to the clinic.
## TRICORDRAZINE
[bold]Orange bottle.[/bold] A gentle general first aid tablet for small injuries of every kind. One tablet. Do not take more than two in a short period.
## IMIDAZOLINE
[bold]Aquamarine bottle.[/bold] For eye strain and eye injury from welding flash, bright flares or dust. One tablet. A mild medicine, but see the clinic if your sight does not return.
## IRON
[bold]Black bottle.[/bold] Helps the body replace lost blood after an injury. Take as your clinician directs.
## TRAVEL PACKETS
Bicaridine, Kelotane and Tricordrazine in a sealed foil packet for a pocket or a first aid pouch. Once a tablet is out, it does not go back in. Do not take more than two in a short period.
